usage.notes: Panacea accesses the openFDA drug-label endpoint only through its canonical server adapter. The optional OPENFDA_KEY remains server-side. Runtime requests are bounded, time-limited and normalized before reaching orchestration/UI layers; consumer modules should not construct openFDA requests directly.

license.identifier: CC0-1.0 / U.S. public-domain policy with documented exceptions
license.scope: openFDA states that its content, data, documentation, code and related materials are generally public domain and released under CC0 1.0 unless otherwise noted. Individual records or fields can contain third-party material that is not covered by CC0 and must retain any explicit warning or separate rights restriction.
license.notes: FDA requests attribution even though it is not generally required. Panacea must not imply FDA endorsement. Any record or field carrying a third-party-rights warning overrides the general CC0 assumption for that material.

validation.notes: openFDA explicitly warns that its data should not be relied on for medical-care decisions and that not all data is validated for clinical or production use. Panacea may present official label content, including mechanism-of-action text when the label supplies it, as reference context rather than patient-specific prescribing advice.

provenance.notes: Preserve the SPL set_id when available, otherwise the openFDA record id, together with the exact key-free source URL when a stable set_id exists, the medication query and retrieval timestamp. A drug name alone is not sufficient provenance because multiple labels can exist for the same ingredient or brand.

adapter.notes: Canonical production adapter performs bounded brand-name lookup with generic-name fallback, uses upstream timeouts, returns selected structured-product-label fields including mechanism_of_action when present, and preserves set_id/record identity plus a key-free source URL when available. Higher-level drugInfo orchestration reuses this adapter rather than issuing duplicate openFDA requests.

trust.notes: High authority for the provenance of FDA-published label records. The evidence-quality dimension is intentionally lower because openFDA itself warns that API data is not a substitute for validated clinical decision support; license clarity is reduced by explicitly documented third-party exceptions.
